gen-fs-oswald-gf-teachers: Confident, tightly knit rows of Oswald sit over Teachers, whose thin, rod-like letters keep their width through every turn. Compressed muscle up top, modern wire below: that difference does the work.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-telex: Telex draws curvy, unclamped letters beneath the tightly knit, confident rows of Oswald. Telex stays clean paragraph after paragraph of running text, its loose curves never crowding one another.
gen-fs-chubbo-dm-sans: Marker-tip letters with a smooth, unobstructed path around every bend make Chubbo feel casual and inviting. DM Sans brings wide-set terminals on its s and a friendly, approachable manner.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-tenor-sans: Oswald hits hard: tightly knit rows, low contrast, all confidence. Tenor Sans keeps its c tips well apart and varies its stroke weight lightly, so running text feels gentle and contemporary.
gen-fs-chubbo-nunito-sans: Smooth as a pen-plotter line, Chubbo goes round every bend like marker ink. Nunito Sans keeps the small letters open-mouthed and soft, so extended reading feels gentle and unhurried.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-tirra: Tightly knit and confident, Oswald comes in like a shout across the top. And Tirra rounds things off, its forms curving like open parentheses in a modern voice.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-titillium-web: Tightly knit rows of confident, strong letters make Oswald feel packed and ready to be seen. Titillium Web does the opposite job, setting stroke ends far apart for a contemporary, approachable texture.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-syncopate: Casual and inviting, Chubbo rolls marker-tip curves along smooth paths, while Syncopate lines up beneath with technical-pen steadiness. Its rope-ladder spacing makes longer text move in measured steps.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-tomorrow: Oswald packs confident, strong letters into tightly knit rows, while Tomorrow opens its bowls like a cupped palm of clay. One squeezes in, the other lets the page breathe.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-switzer: Switzer stands tall in the lowercase, with wire-like letterforms and c tips that never creep toward touching. But Red Hat Display, with its marker-like line and daylight inside every curve, earns its keep when big and short.
